sources.title: Human History Map, imported Laotian states record
sources.note: Current local index and three TopoJSON features decoded. 1650-1783 umbrella; repeated broad polygon does not show the 1707/1713 political divisions. Earlier laos and modern laos-1938 remain separate. Own project factual-data source, not third-party prose.

sources.title: Li Kunrui, “Nanzhang equals Laos”: examining a mistaken identification (Qing History Research, 2009)
sources.note: Original institutional indexed text checked with query site:iqh.ruc.edu.cn "1707" "1713" "南掌". Direct page fails. Passage explains 1707 Luang Prabang/Vientiane split, 1713 Champasak, partly independent Muang Phuan and that Qing tributary Nanzhang was Luang Prabang, not all Laos. No king death date taken from this source.

sources.title: Andrea Matles Savada, editor, Laos: A Country Study (1995)
sources.note: Original indexed PDF checked: Table A chronology, printed xv, and National Security historical background. Direct PDF gives 403. Queries exact title with 1713/1778 and 1828/Vientiane reproduce relevant original text. Only late eighteenth-century Siamese domination and later destruction used; not its inconsistent Sourigna reign dates.

sources.title: Wouter Feldberg, Gerrit Wuijsthoff’s Journey to the Lao Court at Vientiane, 1641-1642
sources.note: Original academic conference abstract hosted by Northern Illinois University read directly. Describes VOC mission from Loveck, trade purpose, Souligna Vongsa court and surviving National Archives journal. Visit precedes atlas start and is labeled background.

sources.title: Pakdeekul Ratana, Social Strategies in Creating Roles for Women in Lan Na and Lan Sang from the Thirteenth to the Nineteenth Centuries (2009)
sources.note: Original Münster dissertation directly read, with local text extraction. Printed page 197, 2008 interview recalling aristocratic women’s eighteenth/nineteenth-century learning; printed page 199, legal evidence of farming/fishing and 1747-1768 Universal History descriptions. Lan Na-only examples excluded; legal texts not precisely dated to one reign.

sources.title: Northern Illinois University SEAsite, Architectural Heritage of Luang Prabang
sources.note: Direct institutional teaching page, paragraphs on raised wooden houses, kitchens, roof/eaves, work/storage space and sleeping orientation. Historical building tradition, not an excavated seventeenth-century house or universal rule for every Lao community.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Town of Luang Prabang
sources.note: Original official description directly read. Sixteenth-century Wat Xieng Thong, urban fabric with village temples, and surviving ponds used for fish and vegetables. Clearly distinguish accumulated/colonial heritage and modern conservation description from securely dated 1650-1783 features.

sources.title: Digital Library of Lao Manuscripts, About the Collection
sources.note: Original library documentation directly read. Palm-leaf dimensions, iron-tipped stylus, soot/oil, cords/covers/wrappings; varied languages, scripts and subject categories. General manuscript tradition, not dates for particular manufacture.

sources.title: Volker Grabowsky, Thai and Lao Manuscript Cultures Revisited (2019)
sources.note: Original Journal of the Siam Society 107(1):79-118 PDF directly read and text extracted. Page 84 Vat Si Mungkhun 1763/64 foundation; page 89 discovery and likely 1662 Vohara manuscript BAD-21-1-0478; pages 96-97 dated 1843 colophon BAD-21-1-0479 f22v, reproduced in modern Thai-script transcription and translated. Original manuscript Tham Lao script. 1783 BAD-21-1-0477 contradictory dating/title avoided. Entire work one budget despite second publisher host.

sources.title: Bethany G. Elkington and colleagues, Folk Epidemiology Recorded in Palm Leaf Manuscripts of Laos (2012)
sources.note: Original Journal of Lao Studies 3(1) article directly read. Pages 7-9 methods and sample entries; critically, page 9 says only three studied manuscripts dated, to 1913, 1948 and 1977, all others undated. Thus health example is later archival comparison, not a measured eighteenth-century disease burden. PMC is the same work, no extra budget.

proposedOverrides.name: Laotian states
proposedOverrides.summary: Late Lan Xang and several successor kingdoms, with distinct courts, communities and changing external pressures.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One standalone plural atlas umbrella; no aliases. Earlier laos (1492-1650) and modern laos-1938 remain separate. Lan Xang unification and successor kingdoms described as distinct political phases.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Three repeated polygons in world-1650, world-1700 and world-1715, bbox [100,13.255980,107.513275,22.534119]. No 1707/1713 internal political boundaries. Point checks separately record principal cities; broad regional outline not proof of royal administration everywhere.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: No exact Sourigna reign dates used because consulted older sources disagree. 1707 split and 1713 Champasak supported by institutional historical study. 1778 onset of Siamese dominance, not 1783 common fall. Later 1828 Vientiane destruction distinguished.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Architecture and medical knowledge have explicitly later or broadly dated witnesses; no uniform family, ethnic, religious or sanitation system inferred. Siam and Vietnamese polities are external powers, not aliases. No newly added geometry or successors.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: 1843 Lao manuscript colophon reproduced only in the scholar’s modern Thai-script transcription, clearly labeled as such. It is later than the map interval. A likely 1662 teaching manuscript is identified, but no unattested wording invented for it.
